original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-fpqc-covering}
Let $S$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to S\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
be a standard fpqc covering of $S$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-standard-fpqc}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.

final_content.statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be affine, and let $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ be a finite standard fpqc covering: each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ is affine, and the map $\coprod_{i=1}^nU_i\to S$ is faithfully flat (equivalently, $R\to\prod_{i=1}^nA_i$ is faithfully flat). Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective and the canonical functor $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh})$ is fully faithful; in fact it is an equivalence.
hypotheses: $S$ is affine and $\mathcal U$ is a finite standard fpqc family of affine schemes with faithfully flat disjoint union over $S$.
conclusions: Every quasi-coherent descent datum is effective, and restriction to the covering is fully faithful.
